document_title: Code of Professional Conduct
notes: IFT is the primary US professional body for food science. Code guides members to consider public benefit, food safety, environmental impacts, and confine advocacy to areas of competence.

organization: Institute of Food Science and Technology
document_title: Code of Professional Conduct
notes: UK equivalent of IFT. Disciplinary process includes possible expulsion. Also cross-listed in IIT Ethics Codes Collection (node/5093). Companion: Guidelines for Ethical and Professional Practices for Sensory Analysis of Foods.

document_title: Code of Ethics for Food Science and Technology Professionals
notes: European food science education network. Explicitly designed as a teaching tool. Key principles: honesty, dignity, conflict-of-interest declaration, confidentiality, professional competence.

organization: Food and Agriculture Organization / World Health Organization
document_title: FAO Expert Consultation on Food Safety: Science and Ethics (Report)
notes: Expert consultation held September 2002, report published 2003. Establishes ethical principles for food safety risk analysis: beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, autonomy, transparency, accountability, participation. Relevant to Codex Alimentarius framework.

document_title: Occupational Safety and Health in the Food and Drink Industries
profession_name: Food and Drink Industry Workers and Employers
notes: ILO sectoral working paper / OSH guidance for food, drink, and tobacco sector. Addresses ergonomics, hazardous substances, biological hazards, machine safety. Developed following ILO Food and Drink Industries Committee resolutions. Also covers Division 11 and 12.

document_title: Code of Conduct (2020) and Marketing and Advertising Code (2008)
notes: Code adopted August 6, 2020. Covers: ethical conduct, lawful cooperation, anti-discrimination, responsible consumption, anti-harassment. Complaint panel includes employment law, DEI, and alcohol beverage law experts. Marketing Code (2008) allows member complaints against other members.

document_title: Code of Ethics
notes: State-level guild ethics code. Commits members to community support, ethical business practices, principles of excellence, equity, and respect. Reinforced through DEI training access. Included as representative of regional craft beverage ethics codes.

document_title: Code of Advertising Standards
notes: Established 1949; continuously updated. Cited as model of effective self-regulation by industry observers. Covers: prohibition of depicting intoxication, no appeals to minors, responsible consumption messaging. 2014 Digital Marketing Guidelines added. FTC has commended the Code.

organization: Distilled Spirits Council of the United States
document_title: Code of Responsible Practices for Beverage Alcohol Advertising and Marketing
notes: 2022 edition. Covers spirits, malt beverages, and wine. Code Review Board adjudicates complaints. 100% member compliance record; FTC-commended. Raises adult audience placement standard to 73.8%. Includes new informal inquiry pathway added in 2022 revision.

document_title: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC)
notes: Adopted by World Health Assembly May 21, 2003; entered into force February 27, 2005. 38 articles. Ethically significant provisions: Article 5.3 (protect public health from industry interference), Article 17 (economically viable alternatives for tobacco workers/growers). Governs the sector externally rather than being an industry self-code.

organization: CORESTA (Cooperation Centre for Scientific Research Relative to Tobacco)
document_title: Best Practices and Guidelines for Research on Tobacco and Nicotine Containing Products
notes: CORESTA founded 1956. Primary outputs are test methods and research guidelines (CROM best practices). ISO TC/126 liaison. No standalone code of ethics found; research standards imply scientific integrity principles. Included as closest available document for this division.

document_title: Better Cotton Standard
notes: 23% of global cotton production as of 2024. Key ethical provisions: prohibition of child labor (<15), prohibition of forced labor, non-discrimination, freedom of association, minimum wage, safe conditions. Prohibition of Highly Hazardous Pesticides (HHPs). Third-party field verification.

document_title: Workplace Code of Conduct and Compliance Benchmarks
notes: Based on ILO standards. ~75% of FLA-audited factories are apparel. Covers: prohibition of forced/child labor, no harassment/abuse, no discrimination, freedom of association, compensation, working hours, health and safety. Independent accreditation process. Also covers Divisions 13 and 15.

document_title: Code of Labour Practices
notes: Dutch NGO founded 1999. 8-point code rooted in UN and ILO standards. Covers: fair wages, reasonable hours, safe/healthy environments, elimination of child labor, freedom of association. Annual Brand Performance Checks publicly reported. Living wages program.

document_title: 12 WRAP Principles
notes: World's largest independent apparel certification program. 12 principles: labor rights (child/forced labor, H&S, harassment, discrimination, hours, compensation, freedom of association), environment, customs compliance, security. Based on ILO conventions. Accepted by Walmart, Disney, Costco, etc. Also covers Divisions 13 and 15.

document_title: Business Social Compliance Initiative (BSCI) Code of Conduct 2.0
notes: Founded 2003. 11 elements including: workers involvement/protection, freedom of association, non-discrimination, fair remuneration, decent working hours, health and safety, prohibition of child/forced labor, environment, and ethical business behavior. Grounded in UDHR, UNGP, ILO, OECD Guidelines, UN Global Compact. Biennial audit validity. Also covers Divisions 13, 15, 16.

document_title: THREADS Protocol / Social Responsibility Program
notes: AAFA is the primary US trade group for apparel and footwear. THREADS Protocol is their sustainability and social responsibility policy framework for regulatory engagement. Official CSR partner: WRAP. Social Responsibility Committee coordinates industry best practice sharing. No standalone ethics document found.

organization: IndustriALL Global Union / UNI Global Union
document_title: International Accord for Health and Safety in the Textile and Garment Industry (2021)
notes: Successor to the 2013 Bangladesh Accord (post-Rana Plaza). 200+ brands signed. Covers: freedom of association, independent safety inspections, worker complaint mechanism, safety committee training. Legally binding. Expanding to Pakistan and other countries. Also covers Division 13.

document_title: Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Textiles, Clothing, Leather and Footwear (2021)
profession_name: Textiles / Clothing / Leather / Footwear Workers and Employers
notes: First-ever ILO code of practice for this sector. Adopted October 2021. Covers 60+ million workers. Addresses biological hazards, hazardous substances, ergonomics, physical hazards, machine/equipment safety, building and fire safety. Worker participation as 'essential element.' Also covers Divisions 13 and 15.

document_title: LWG Audit Standard (Protocol 7) / LWG Sustainability System
notes: Founded 2005. 400+ stakeholders. Protocol 7 introduced social compliance as a non-critical scoring section in 2021; being elevated to critical in next update. Forthcoming LWG Sustainability System adds Manufacturing Standard, Chain of Custody, and Deforestation Due Diligence. Gold/Silver/Bronze/Audited ratings. Covers bovine, caprine, porcine, ovine leathers.

document_title: FSC Principles and Criteria for Forest Stewardship (FSC-STD-01-001 v5-2)
profession_name: Forest Manager / Wood Products Supply Chain
notes: 10 Principles, 70 Criteria. Ethical dimensions: Principle 2 (worker wellbeing), Principle 3 (Indigenous Peoples' legal/customary rights), Principle 4 (local community wellbeing), Principle 6 (ecosystem services). ISEAL Code of Good Practice compliant since 2006. Cross-listed with Division 17 (paper products).

document_title: SFI Standard (2022)
profession_name: Forest Manager / Wood Products Supply Chain
notes: Originally established by AF&PA in 1994; spun off as independent 2010. World's largest single forest certification standard by area. 13 Principles, 15 Objectives, 37 Performance Measures, 101 Indicators. Key ethical aspects: land stewardship ethic, Indigenous Peoples' rights, community involvement, biodiversity protection. PEFC-endorsed. Cross-listed with Division 17.

organization: Technical Association of the Pulp and Paper Industry
document_title: TAPPI Code of Ethics
profession_name: Pulp, Paper, and Converting Industry Professional
notes: ~14,000 members globally. Code covers: fair treatment of employees, avoiding unauthorized intrusion into competitors' business, cooperative knowledge sharing, honest assessment of client/employer work, integrity in technical publications (no exaggeration/misrepresentation). Contact: Mary Beth Cornell, mcornell@tappi.org.

document_title: Code of Conduct
notes: Result of merger of Printing Industries of America (PIA) and SGIA. Code covers: upholding highest ethical standards, paramount public safety and welfare, professional honor/integrity/dignity, non-discrimination (race, sex/gender identity, religion, disability, etc.), intellectual tolerance. Enforcement: reprimand or loss of membership/volunteer role.

document_title: Ethical Responsibility and Professional and Personal Conduct Code
notes: Applies to AFPM members and non-member attendees at AFPM meetings. Requirements: antitrust compliance, adherence to federal/state law, highest professional/ethical behavior, working to build public confidence in refining/petrochemical industries. First offense: informal censure by Executive Committee. Continued violations: expulsion from AFPM (Board of Directors). Downstream/refining counterpart to API (captured in ISIC Section B).
